$comment: This file is the only description of the backend that this repository is allowed to rely on.
It is a SNAPSHOT, not a live read: platform-backend is a different repository on a different
deploy cadence, and an intern working here has no way to notice that a field was renamed over
there. So the shapes are written down, stamped with the commit they were read from, and a test
asserts the local mock still matches them.
That gives drift a place to show up. It does NOT detect drift on its own - nothing here can
see the other repository. Re-derive it with `npm run contract:derive -- <path-to-platform-backend>`
whenever you touch this feature, and treat a diff as a conversation with the backend owner
rather than a merge conflict to resolve locally.

auth.note: A short-lived HMAC capability token scoped to ONE attempt at ONE booking. The reservation id is taken FROM THE TOKEN, never from a body. The backend declares token_scope_mismatch for a body id that disagrees, but at the snapshot commit no route passes one to the check, so the word is never emitted. The attempt_id is the ledger's call key: see the call-event route's ledger block. Never put the token in a query string - carrier and proxy logs retain URLs.
auth.dark_when: VENUE_CALL_SECRET unset on the backend. Every route then refuses seam_disabled.

token.hmac: sha256 over "<reservation_id>.<attempt_id>.<expiry_ms>", base64url, key = VENUE_CALL_SECRET as utf8
token.note: Only TWO refusal words, deliberately: a refusal that says WHY tells a prober which half of their guess was right. An unparseable token, a forged signature and a token edited to name another booking (so its signature no longer matches) all return invalid. A correctly signed token for another booking is NOT refused: it opens that booking. So each call must hold only its own token.

routes.when: once, in the gap between the carrier answering and the first word
during the call, once per question the opening lines do not already answer
routes.note: `say` is a FINISHED SENTENCE and is always present, including when known is false. `reason` appears only when known is false.

routes.when: during the call, before speaking any deferral

request_body.question_verbatim: string, max 1000, VERBATIM not a paraphrase - optional

routes.note: asked_to_stop_calling is written SYNCHRONOUSLY before this responds. `say` is empty string for answerer_reported - the agent says nothing, it is a report to us.

ledger.note: ONE ledger row per call. The row in reservation_call_attempts is keyed by call_id = the attempt_id inside the token. The first event of a call writes the row; every later event of the same call folds into it (its note is appended) and the disposition only moves UP disposition_rank, so a late, weaker event can never undo a stop. A re-dial is a new call and MUST carry a token minted with a NEW attempt_id: reuse one and the second call's events fold into the first call's row, and the 3-per-day attempt count never sees it.

refusal.why_409: These are not authentication outcomes to retry differently. They mean the call cannot proceed, and the agent's only correct response to every one is to stop before speaking.

campaign_rule.note: An ALLOW-LIST, read from the backend's CALL_KEEPING_CAMPAIGN_STATUSES. A booking on an active or paused campaign is called; every other status - including NULL and any word not in known_statuses - refuses campaign_not_active before a word is spoken. Paused is allowed because pausing stops new outreach, not visits already booked: the guest is still coming and the venue still needs the notice. known_statuses is the backend's campaign status vocabulary, carried so a NEW status shows up as drift - it would refuse by default, which is safe, but somebody should decide.

known_divergences.what: comp_terms has no authored clause to return on the deployed backend yet, so it always returns the honest refusal.
known_divergences.mock_default: Scenario `happy` reproduces today: comp_terms refuses with reason not_agreed. Scenario `comp-known` returns an authored clause, which is what the comp-clause backend change delivers.
known_divergences.why: Both branches must be exercised. Today's is the one deployed; tomorrow's is the one being built.
